sources.citation: Menanti, Jacqualine and Ben Rumaropen. 2022. Survey Report on the Kapauri Language of Papua, Indonesia. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2022-026. Dallas: SIL International. 69 pp. (survey trip May 2006; Appendix B.2 wordlists incl. Kosare [kiq] of Muara Nawa and of Naira).
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: No phonology section. The only prosodic information is the per-word stress marks in the two 239-item Kosare field wordlists (Muara Nawa; Naira-at-Pagai), explicitly flagged as unanalysed field transcriptions. Sociolinguistic text notes Kapauri speakers in Pagai also speak Kosare; nothing on Kosare sound system.

sources.citation: Palmer, Bill. 2019. Kaure and its relatives: a language family of West Papua's eastern Lakes Plain. One-page abstract submitted to the 5th Workshop on the Languages of Papua (WLP5), Manokwari, July 2019 (PDF uploaded with the WLP5 abstracts on indoling.com, 2019-03; not in the final program). Precursor of Palmer 2020 MS 'The phylogenetic status of the Kaure languages of northeastern West Papua' (Glottolog ref 581393).
sources.note: No prosody at all. Content: classification history (Voorhoeve 1975, Wurm 1982, Silzer & Clouse 1991, Foley 2017, Pawley & Hammarstrom 2017), 13 doculects compared, regular segmental sound correspondences (e.g. Sause *k>glottal stop /V_V, *s>h word-initially, loss of final vowels; *u>y in Harna/Lereh; *r>l etc.), a Kaure-Kosare vs Kapauri-Sause branching, Kapauri-Kosare contact ('ear' loan), Table 1 with Kosare forms sroto 'one', koro/woru' 'ear', paka' 'moon' (no stress marks), proto-form reconstruction announced, no TNG link. Nothing on stress, accent, tone or syllable structure for Kosare o…

sources.note: Nothing for Kosare. The Appendix intro only says the Kosare transcription is 'somewhat narrower'; the 97-item Kosare list carries per-word stress marks ('kako 'bone', 'tomo 'black', kora'fe 'one', o'reka 'kill', to'wai 'know') but no rule is stated.
